task.description: WF-02 Step 3 for REQ-134, resubmitted after TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 (handoffs/WF02-REQ134-20260823/step4-test-run.json, commit bb78e56): AC3's reset-then-baseline fix (rework 2, previously PASSED at step3b and routed to Step 4) held up under a real live Keycloak, but AC2's assertion did not -- it asserted exact map equality on the tampered-token 401 response body, which fails against the real response because AuthPipeline.reject/4 (pre-existing, unrelated to this suite) always includes a 'detail' key alongside 'error'. Fixing that assertion bug and resubmitting for a fresh Step 3b pass before returning to Step 4.
acceptance_criteria: a test obtains a genuine token from the running Keycloak and drives it through Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline end to end, with the real assertion output quoted
the token's signature is verified against the live JWKS via the real verifier, not TokenVerifierDouble -- demonstrated by the test failing if pointed at a tampered token
JIT provisioning creates a real user row on first authentication and reuses it on the second, asserted across two calls
the default mix test run still passes with Keycloak stopped, quoted as evidence
the real-token tests skip with a message naming exactly what must be running, rather than failing obscurely
the result states the exact command a developer runs to execute them

result.summary:
Fixed the BLOCKER from step4-test-run.json: test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs's AC2 test asserted `Jason.decode!(conn.resp_body) == %{"error" => "unauthorized"}` (exact map equality). Read lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex's reject/4 (line ~322) myself to confirm: it unconditionally encodes both `error` and `detail` keys on every rejection, so exact equality against a single-key map can never hold for a real response. Read the sibling test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs:196 to confirm the established convention for this exact situation: `assert %{"error" => "unauthorized"} = Jason.decode!(conn.resp_body)` -- a partial pattern match, not full equality. Mirrored that pattern exactly in the AC2 test, with a comment explaining why (reject/4's extra 'detail' key, cited to the sibling test's own line number).

test/specs/REQ-134.md's AC2 section updated to describe the partial-match assertion instead of exact equality, citing the sibling test's pattern and recording this correction with today's date so a future reader sees why the wording changed.

mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force (MIX_ENV=test): PASSED CLEAN -- 'Compiling 131 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', zero warnings, zero errors.

This environment had a real, reachable Keycloak (TEST-RUNNER's own container, letflow-keycloak-1 on port 8093, this workspace's .env already pointing at it -- confirmed via `docker compose ps` showing it Up (healthy) alongside postgres), so I did NOT need to defer live verification to TEST-RUNNER this round -- ran it myself for real, twice in a row against the SAME persistent database, to directly confirm both this AC2 fix and the AC3 reset-then-baseline repeatability fix together:

  $ mix test --include keycloak test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs
  ...
  Finished in 3.1 seconds (0.00s async, 3.1s sync)
  Result: 3 passed

  $ mix test --include keycloak test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs   (second consecutive run, same database)
  ...
  Finished in 1.1 seconds (0.00s async, 1.1s sync)
  Result: 3 passed

Both runs: 3/3 passed. The second run is the direct, executed proof that AC3's reset-then-baseline fix (rework 2) is genuinely repeatable across invocations against a persistent database, not merely reasoned about -- the exact property step3b's own re-derivation checked by inspection is now also checked by execution.

AC4 default-exclusion re-confirmed with Keycloak now running (not stopped, unlike the prior submission -- confirms the exclusion is a test_helper.exs config default independent of Keycloak's runtime state, matching step4's own finding): `mix test test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs` -> 'Excluding tags: [:keycloak]' / 'Result: 0 tests, 3 excluded'.

AC5's raise-vs-skip mechanism, KeycloakTestClient, test_helper.exs's exclusion default: untouched, unchanged from the already-validated prior state.

Developer command for AC6 (unchanged, re-verified accurate and now also verified to actually work end to end): mix test --include keycloak test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs

gate_history.summary: AC1/AC2/AC4/AC6 pass; AC5's raise-vs-skip deviation independently re-derived and ruled compliant. gate_history.summary: AC1/AC2/AC4/AC6 re-confirmed; AC5's ruling from iteration 0 stands. Rework-1's baseline-diff fix (count_before, asserting count_before+1 twice) did NOT eliminate the defect -- it moved it. Root cause: lib/letflow/identity.ex's upsert_by_external_identity/4 is a genuine find-or-create, so on a second invocation of the same persistent database, count_before was captured as 1 (the row surviving from run 1), and the post-call-1 count stayed at count_before rather than count_before + 1.
issues: AC3's count_before baseline is captured from live, un-reset database state, so the second and later invocations fail deterministically.
gate_history.next_action: Rework TEST-DESIGNER: reset this subject's row to a true, invocation-independent zero before capturing any baseline, then assert the original 0 -> 1 -> 1 sequence. Rework iteration 2 of 3 -- the last one before this run must escalate.

All other Step 3b criteria re-checked and passed. AC4 re-verified with Keycloak stopped: 'Excluding tags: [:keycloak]' / 'Result: 0 tests, 3 excluded'.
